question.problem: By the multiplicative property of congruences, $95\cdot 109≡$
question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}95 & ≡11\cdot 8+7\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡11\cdot 0+7\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡7\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\ 109 & ≡13\cdot 8+5\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡13\cdot 0+5\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}95\cdot 109 & ≡7\cdot 5\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡35\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡4\cdot 8+3\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡4\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
95\cdot 109≡3\,(\text{mod}\,8).
$$
